High tidal waves crash R.K. Beach in Visakhapatnam on Thursday, amid rough sea conditions under the influence of Cyclone Akvan.
| Photo Credit: K.R. DEEPAK
Even as the severe cyclonic storm Akvan may spare most of Andhra Pradesh and make landfall along the south Odisha coast near Gopalpur on November 20, the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, has put the Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts bordering Odisha on a red alert.
Between 8.30 a.m. and 7 p.m. on Thursday, many weather stations in Srikakulam district recorded only light to moderate rain of below 35 mm. However, IMD, Amaravati, Director K. Naga Ratnam told The Hindu that the rainfall may increase from the midnight and may continue till Friday noon or evening. Isolated extremely heavy rainfall is likely in these two districts.
Gales of 90 kmph to 100 kmph are also likely along the coast in North Coastal Andhra Pradesh around the midnight. Already, strong winds of 50 kmph to 60 kmph are prevailing along the coast, the Director said.
Parvathipuram-Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Anakapalli districts may also record isolated very heavy rainfall till Friday evening, but the rest of the State may not see any rainfall activity on Friday.
Weather experts said while the weather system may move closer to the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha, which is around 180 km from Srikakulam, there is a slight possibility of the system making landfall near the extreme end of North Coastal Andhra Pradesh as well.
Meanwhile, as per the latest bulletin issued by the IMD at 5.30 p.m., Akvan moved northwards with the speed of 13 kmph till 2.30 p.m. and remained over the west-central Bay of Bengal, which is about 390 km east-southeast of Narsapur and 320 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam of Andhra Pradesh, 410 km south of Gopalpur and 470 km south of Puri of Odisha and 610 km east-northeast of Chennai of Tamil Nadu.
It is likely to move north-northwestwards and cross the coast close to Gopalpur by Friday noon, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90kmph to 100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph.
A storm surge of 0.5 to 1.0 metre height above the astronomical tide is very likely to inundate low-lying areas along the coastal belt in the districts of Kakinada, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and Visakhapatnam districts, the IMD said in its bulletin.
Published - November 20, 2026 12:09 am IST
